pr.body:
# Fix: Update InsightsBookingService integration tests for Prisma.sql format ## Summary This PR updates the `InsightsBookingService` integration tests to work with the new Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation. The changes follow the exact same testing patterns established in the `InsightsRoutingService` integration tests. **Key Changes:** - Replace Prisma object notation expectations with direct `Prisma.sql` template literal comparisons - Add `NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0`` constant for consistency with other services - Update all authorization and filter condition tests to expect raw SQL instead of object structures - Modify the final integration test to use `$queryRaw` for actual database querying - Remove complex object notation assertions in favor of direct SQL comparisons ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human ⚠️ **HIGH RISK** - This involves SQL query construction and authorization logic - [ ] **Run integration tests manually** - I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass: `TZ=UTC yarn test packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` - [ ] **Review SQL query construction** - Carefully examine the authorization conditions in the service, especially complex team/org scope logic with AND/OR combinations - [ ] **Verify authorization security** - Test with different user roles (owner, admin, member) to ensure no privilege escalation bugs - [ ] **Check parameter binding** - Ensure all user inputs in the SQL templates are properly parameterized (no injection risks) - [ ] **Test edge cases** - Verify behavior with empty teams, missing users, null values, and boundary conditions **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Run the integration tests locally to verify they pass 2. Test the service with various user roles and team configurations 3. Verify the `$queryRaw` integration test actually queries the database correctly 4. Check that authorization conditions properly restrict access based on user permissions --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD Service["packages/lib/server/service/
insightsBooking.ts"]:::context Tests["packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/
insightsBooking.integration-test.ts"]:::major-edit RoutingTests["InsightsRoutingService
integration tests
(attachment example)"]:::context Service --> Tests RoutingTests --> Tests Tests --> AuthTests["Authorization Condition Tests
- NOTHING_CONDITION
- User/Team/Org scope"]:::major-edit Tests --> FilterTests["Filter Condition Tests
- Event type filtering
- Member user filtering"]:::major-edit Tests --> IntegrationTest["Database Integration Test
- $queryRaw usage
- Real query execution"]:::major-edit subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - This conversion was based on the InsightsRoutingService integration test patterns provided in the user's attachment - The test runner had configuration issues during development, so manual verification of test execution is critical - All test expectations now use direct `Prisma.sql` comparisons instead of inspecting `.strings` and `.values` properties - The NOTHING_CONDITION constant ensures consistency across different insight services **Session Info:** Requested by @eunjae-lee | Session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a5e216ec6c364679a220f799e2abc700
pr.title: feat: convert InsightsBookingService to use Prisma.sql raw queries

raw_findings.body: TypeScript accepts the call (teamId is optional in the new public type), but `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse` fails at runtime, `this.options` becomes null, and every query silently degrades to `1=0`, returning zero rows instead of the team's bookings.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Type-level guarantee lost; invalid option combinations compile and fail silently at runtime as an empty result set.
raw_findings.impact: TypeScript accepts the call (teamId is optional in the new public type), but `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse` fails at runtime, `this.options` becomes null, and every query silently degrades to `1=0`, returning zero rows instead of the team's bookings.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch replaced the zod-derived discriminated union in the constructor signature with a hand-written flat type whose discriminant no longer constrains the other fields.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the constructor parameter typed as the discriminated `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (or derive the public type from the schema with `z.input<typeof insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema>`) so a missing `teamId` for `scope: "team"` is a compile error.
raw_findings.title: Constructor options type widened to a non-discriminated shape, hiding missing teamId at compile time
raw_findings.trigger: A caller constructs `new InsightsBookingService({ prisma, options: { scope: "team", userId, orgId } })` without `teamId`.

raw_findings.body: The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches are dead code today, and the dead branch encodes a WHERE clause built from user-supplied filters with no authorization predicate — if authorization ever returns an empty/falsy Sql it would expose all rows of BookingTimeStatusDenormalized.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead, misleading control flow that encodes an auth-less query path.
raw_findings.impact: The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches are dead code today, and the dead branch encodes a WHERE clause built from user-supplied filters with no authorization predicate — if authorization ever returns an empty/falsy Sql it would expose all rows of BookingTimeStatusDenormalized.
raw_findings.root_cause: The rewrite treats the non-nullable `Prisma.Sql` authorization result as if it could be null/empty, producing branches that can never execute but that would bypass authorization semantics if reached.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Drop the truthiness test on `authConditions` (it is non-nullable): return `Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})`` when filters exist, otherwise return `authConditions`; remove the filter-only and NOTHING fallbacks.
raw_findings.title: Unreachable truthiness branches in getBaseConditions include a filter-only path that omits authorization
raw_findings.trigger: Any call to `getBaseConditions()`; `getAuthorizationConditions()` is typed `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy.

raw_findings.body: A regression in the memoization (e.g. caching `null` incorrectly so the `undefined` sentinel check re-builds on every call, or returning a stale Sql after filters change) would ship undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Coverage loss for still-live service behavior.
raw_findings.impact: A regression in the memoization (e.g. caching `null` incorrectly so the `undefined` sentinel check re-builds on every call, or returning a stale Sql after filters change) would ship undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch removed the `Caching` describe block while converting expectations instead of porting it to the Prisma.sql assertions.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two caching tests, updated to the new `Prisma.Sql` expectations (assert the second call returns a value deep-equal to the first for both authorization and filter conditions).
raw_findings.title: Caching test suite deleted although the caching code path remains in the service
raw_findings.trigger: Running the integration suite after this patch: `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` memoization in `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` is still implemented but no longer exercised by any test.

raw_findings.body: `Array.prototype.reduce` called without an initial value seeds the accumulator with element 0 and starts the callback at index 1, so the guard never runs; it is dead code that suggests the author expected index 0 to be visited and invites a future edit that adds an initial value and silently drops the first condition.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead branch and duplicated fragile join logic in three places.
raw_findings.impact: `Array.prototype.reduce` called without an initial value seeds the accumulator with element 0 and starts the callback at index 1, so the guard never runs; it is dead code that suggests the author expected index 0 to be visited and invites a future edit that adds an initial value and silently drops the first condition.
raw_findings.root_cause: The SQL-joining helper was written assuming reduce iterates from index 0 even though no initial accumulator is supplied.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the hand-rolled reducers with `Prisma.join(conditions, " AND ")` / `Prisma.join(conditions, " OR ")` (already used elsewhere in the repo), or delete the unreachable `index === 0` check.
raw_findings.title: Unreachable `index === 0` guard inside reduce without an initial value
raw_findings.trigger: Any invocation of `buildFilterConditions()` with at least one filter (same pattern is repeated in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`).

raw_findings.body: The two authorization tests fail with an opaque Sql deep-equality diff even though behavior is unchanged, and the tests never assert against the service's real constant.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Brittle test coupled to a duplicated literal rather than the module contract.
raw_findings.impact: The two authorization tests fail with an opaque Sql deep-equality diff even though behavior is unchanged, and the tests never assert against the service's real constant.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch copied the private service constant into the test file, duplicating a value that must stay in sync.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Export `NOTHING_CONDITION` from `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` and import it in the test instead of duplicating the literal.
raw_findings.title: Test re-declares the service's NOTHING sentinel instead of importing it
raw_findings.trigger: Someone changes the sentinel in `insightsBooking.ts` (e.g. to `Prisma.sql`1 = 0`` or `FALSE`).

raw_findings.body: No test executes the composed SQL for a non-owner/invalid-options user, so a future change that makes `NOTHING_CONDITION` non-restrictive (or drops the auth clause from `getBaseConditions`) would still pass CI while leaking every booking row.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorization regression in raw SQL composition would go undetected by the suite.
raw_findings.impact: No test executes the composed SQL for a non-owner/invalid-options user, so a future change that makes `NOTHING_CONDITION` non-restrictive (or drops the auth clause from `getBaseConditions`) would still pass CI while leaking every booking row.
raw_findings.root_cause: The converted integration test only ported the positive `findMany` assertion and did not add a negative-authorization case for the new raw-SQL composition.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a case in the `getBaseConditions` describe where the caller is not an org owner/admin, run the same `$queryRaw` and assert the result set is empty.
raw_findings.title: New getBaseConditions raw-query test covers only the authorized path
raw_findings.trigger: Running the suite: the only test under this describe uses an org OWNER with user scope and asserts one matching row is returned.

validated_findings.impact: No test executes the composed SQL for a non-owner/invalid-options user, so a future change that makes `NOTHING_CONDITION` non-restrictive (or drops the auth clause from `getBaseConditions`) would still pass CI while leaking every booking row.
validated_findings.root_cause: The converted integration test only ported the positive `findMany` assertion and did not add a negative-authorization case for the new raw-SQL composition.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a case in the `getBaseConditions` describe where the caller is not an org owner/admin, run the same `$queryRaw` and assert the result set is empty.
validated_findings.title: New getBaseConditions raw-query test covers only the authorized path
validated_findings.trigger: Running the suite: the only test under this describe uses an org OWNER with user scope and asserts one matching row is returned.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that no negative-authorization test exists is speculative about test coverage gaps. The test at line 437-501 does test getBaseConditions with an authorized user. The absence of a specific negative test case is a coverage preference, not a concrete defect introduced by this patch.
